title: parametric-safety-adopter-for-batch-kv-recommendations
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an automated, provably-safe auto-apply path for Optimize recommendations (batching + KV cache heuristics) that uses a parametric safety model to gate rollout, enforce canary policies, and surface operator approval when required. The goal is to reduce manual toil while keeping predictable SLO behavior and fast rollback when regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Auto-apply engine can take a recommendation bundle and instantiate a parametric canary plan (traffic fractions, time windows, and metric gates).
2) Canary scheduler enforces (initialFraction=0.5%, stepDoubling every 30m, maxFraction=20%) and evaluates SLO and quality deltas against baselines.
3) Automatic halt and rollback triggers: latency +5% p50 or +10% p95, error rate +0.25pp, quality drop (prompt-level regression) flagged by eval harness.
4) When projected cost savings exceed 12% and all canary checks pass for 4 consecutive windows, the system will: (a) if savings < 25% then require operator approval; (b) if savings >= 25% then require operator approval and security review.
5) Dashboard and runbook links present in every enactment; audit log contains before/after configs, telemetry snapshots, and actor (system/operator).
6) End-to-end e2e test and simulation harness reproduces staged rollout with synthetic traffic and asserts rollbacks occur when thresholds are violated.
tasks: Design parametric safety model and gate rules (SLO delta equations, hysteresis, minimum sample size)
Implement canary scheduler with fractional traffic routing and timed step progression
Wire telemetry queries for latency/error/throughput and quality evals (prompt sample set)
Create rollback executor that reinstates prior config and triggers notifications
Add operator approval workflow and escalation rules in Console
Add e2e simulation harness and unit/integration tests
Produce runbook and dashboard panels (Console and Grafana links)
progress_updates: 2025-03-02: kick-off meeting with PM and Design; agreed on parametric approach vs fixed stage plan (avoids brittle thresholds)
2025-03-04: safety model draft completed — uses Bayesian confidence intervals on p95 latency and Wilson bounds for error rate; shared in doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=doc-parametric-safety
2025-03-06: PoC canary scheduler implemented (traffic fractioning + step timer). Local e2e sim shows stable behavior for synthetic workloads.
2025-03-09: integrated eval harness for prompt-level quality checks; initial false-positive tuning required (reduced sensitivity on low-frequency prompts)
2025-03-12: first internal canary run against staging with Replay traffic; observed a transient +3% p95 spike that self-resolved — added hysteresis rule to avoid noisy rollbacks

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: noisy metrics causing spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: hysteresis windows + minimum sample sizes + aggregated session-based sampling.
Risk: misestimation of cost savings for multi-model routes. Mitigation: conservative savings projection algorithm and operator approval gate above threshold.
Risk: private deployments require extra approvals. Mitigation: enforce security_review_required and surface KMS access scope in approval flow.
rollback_playbook: 1) Canary hit rollback trigger -> automatic immediate traffic revert to prior config; 2) Generate incident card with snapshot of canary window and diff; 3) Notify on-call + ops channel and open a postmortem stub; 4) If rollback was due to quality regression, tag the recommendation as quarantined and require offline evaluation before re-enqueue.
qa_plan: Unit tests for scheduler step progression, integration test with routing middleware that simulates fractional traffic, golden-run e2e simulation with synthetic traces that assert rollback triggers. Nightly randomized sims to detect edge cases.
next_steps: Land canary scheduler PR, add operator approval modal, run 7 consecutive staging canaries against diverse workloads, and schedule security review for private deployment auto-apply path. Target: 2025-03-28 for GA gating feature flag rollout.
